message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School before being selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers, winning four NBA championships (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2020) and earning numerous MVP awards.

Beyond his on‑court success, LeBron is known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron—and his outspoken advocacy on social justice issues. He has also built a significant media empire, including production deals with companies like Netflix and his own entertainment company, SpringHill Entertainment.
